free_text: The patient is a 66-year-old male with a high PSA of 12.0 and a biopsy-confirmed Gleason 4+3 (ISUP Grade Group 3) adenocarcinoma localized to the mid-left peripheral zone (cT1c). The MRI showed a PI-RADS 3 lesion. Given the high-risk pathological finding and rising PSA trend, treatment decision requires clinical review to weigh potential treatment benefit against the trade-off of potential side effects.
